# duploai_azure_node_pool (Data Source)

Manages a node pool (AKS agent pool) on an Azure Kubernetes Service cluster, provisioned within an environment and resource group.

The pool is created on the AKS cluster linked to the resource group, so that resource group must already have a cluster attached and the cluster must have finished provisioning — the API rejects the create otherwise. Every pool is created as a `User` pool backed by a virtual machine scale set; the cluster's own system pool is not managed here.

The platform stores the pool's configuration and sends the whole of it to Azure on every change, so Terraform sends every field back on update, not just the ones that changed. Nothing in this resource surfaces live Azure state such as the current node count or Kubernetes version: the API deliberately withholds the raw cloud snapshot from its responses, so only `arm_resource_id` and the platform's own status are available. The record's version counter and last-updated timestamp are not exposed either — the API refreshes its cloud snapshot on every read and saves the record as it does, so both change on every GET and would report drift on every plan while meaning nothing.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Look up an existing Azure node pool.
data "duploai_azure_node_pool" "workers" {
  workspace_id = "<workspace-id>"
  id           = "<node-pool-id>"
}

output "vm_size" {
  value = data.duploai_azure_node_pool.workers.vm_size
}

# Sizing as the platform has it recorded. While enable_auto_scaling is true the live node
# count is whatever Azure has scaled to, which this does not report — the API withholds
# the raw cloud snapshot from its responses, so only min_count and max_count are
# meaningful here.
output "sizing" {
  value = {
    node_count          = data.duploai_azure_node_pool.workers.node_count
    min_count           = data.duploai_azure_node_pool.workers.min_count
    max_count           = data.duploai_azure_node_pool.workers.max_count
    enable_auto_scaling = data.duploai_azure_node_pool.workers.enable_auto_scaling
  }
}

# The AKS cluster hosting the pool.
output "cluster" {
  value = "${data.duploai_azure_node_pool.workers.azure_cluster_name} in ${data.duploai_azure_node_pool.workers.azure_cluster_resource_group_name}"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) ID of the object to look up.
- `workspace_id` (String) ID of the workspace that owns this node pool.

### Read-Only

- `allocation_tag` (String) Workload allocation tag for the pool. The platform turns it into an `allocationtags` node label, which is how a service is pinned to these nodes. Must be a valid Kubernetes label value: at most 63 characters of letters, digits, dashes, underscores and dots, starting and ending alphanumeric. Clearing it removes the label.
- `arm_resource_id` (String) Full Azure resource ID (ARM ID) of the node pool, as reported after creation.
- `availability_zones` (List of String) Availability zones the pool spreads its nodes across, e.g. `["1", "2", "3"]`. Left unset, the pool is not zone-spanning. Only zones the region actually offers are accepted. Immutable after creation.
- `azure_cluster_name` (String) Name of the AKS managed cluster in Azure that hosts this pool.
- `azure_cluster_resource_group_name` (String) Azure resource group that owns the AKS managed cluster. Note this is the cluster's resource group, which is not necessarily the one named by `resource_group_id`.
- `cluster_id` (String) ID of the cluster this pool belongs to, taken from the resource group's linked cluster when the pool is created.
- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the node pool was created (RFC 3339).
- `enable_auto_scaling` (Boolean) Let the AKS cluster autoscaler size the pool between `min_count` and `max_count`. While enabled, `node_count` has no effect.
- `environment_id` (String) ID of the environment in which the node pool is provisioned.
- `max_count` (Number) Upper bound for the autoscaler. Only meaningful when `enable_auto_scaling` is true, and must then be greater than or equal to `min_count`.
- `max_pods_per_node` (Number) Maximum pods that may be scheduled on each node. Immutable after creation, and bounded by the cluster's network plugin — the practical ceiling is 250, and Azure CNI reserves an IP address per pod, so a high value needs a subnet large enough to cover `max_pods_per_node` × nodes.
- `min_count` (Number) Lower bound for the autoscaler. Only meaningful when `enable_auto_scaling` is true, and must then be at least 1.
- `name` (String) Node pool name. 1-12 characters, lowercase letters and digits only — no hyphens, underscores or capitals. A Windows pool is limited to 6 characters, which Azure enforces. Immutable after creation.
- `node_count` (Number) Number of nodes in the pool. Ignored while `enable_auto_scaling` is true — Azure then drives the count itself between `min_count` and `max_count`, and a value set here is not applied.

Named `node_count` rather than `count` because `count` is a reserved Terraform meta-argument.
- `node_labels` (Map of String) Kubernetes labels applied to every node in the pool. The platform adds its own `resourcegroup`, `environment`, `workspace` and `allocationtags` labels so that pods can target these nodes; those are filtered out of state and always win over a value set here, so use `allocation_tag` rather than writing the `allocationtags` label directly.
- `node_pool_id` (String) ID of this node pool, for reference by dependent resources.
- `node_taints` (Attributes List) Kubernetes taints applied to every node in the pool, so only pods with a matching toleration are scheduled there. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--node_taints))
- `os_sku` (String) Specific OS image for the pool's nodes. Left unset, Azure picks the default for `os_type` — currently Ubuntu for Linux and Windows2022 for Windows. Must match `os_type`: the Windows SKUs are only valid on a Windows pool, `Ubuntu` and `AzureLinux` only on a Linux one. Immutable after creation.
- `os_type` (String) Operating system for the pool's nodes. Immutable after creation. A `Windows` pool additionally caps `name` at 6 characters.
- `provisioner_type` (String) Provisioner type. Assigned by the platform when unset.
- `provisioner_version` (String) Optional provisioner version. Left unset the API omits it, so this reads back empty rather than as an empty string.
- `resource_group_id` (String) ID of the resource group in which the node pool is provisioned. The AKS cluster the pool joins is the one linked to this resource group.
- `scale_set_priority` (String) Pricing tier for the pool's scale set. `Spot` nodes cost less but Azure can evict them at any time, so keep interruption-tolerant workloads on them only. Immutable after creation.
- `scope_ids` (List of String) Scope IDs linking this node pool to a cloud provider account, inherited from the resource group.
- `status` (String) Current provisioning status of the node pool.
- `unique_cloud_resource_id` (String) Full Azure resource ID (ARM ID) of the node pool, as the platform records it on the resource itself. It is what the delete and refresh operations use to reach the pool. `arm_resource_id` exposes the same ID as reported after creation.
- `upgrade_settings` (Attributes) How aggressively Azure rolls nodes during an upgrade. At most one of surge or unavailable may be active: the API rejects a setting where both are greater than zero. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--upgrade_settings))
- `vm_size` (String) Azure VM size for the pool's nodes, e.g. `Standard_DS2_v2`. Immutable after creation — Azure has no way to resize an existing pool, so changing this replaces it. Which sizes are available depends on the subscription and region.

<a id="nestedatt--node_taints"></a>
### Nested Schema for `node_taints`

Read-Only:

- `effect` (String) What the taint does to pods that do not tolerate it. `NoSchedule` keeps new pods off the node, `PreferNoSchedule` avoids it when possible, and `NoExecute` also evicts pods already running there.
- `key` (String) Taint key.
- `value` (String) Taint value.


<a id="nestedatt--upgrade_settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `upgrade_settings`

Read-Only:

- `max_surge_type` (String) How `max_surge_value` is read. `Default` leaves surge to Azure and ignores the value.
- `max_surge_value` (Number) Extra nodes Azure may add during an upgrade — a node count, or a percentage of the pool between 0 and 100. Required when `max_surge_type` is not `Default`.
- `max_unavailable_type` (String) How `max_unavailable_value` is read. `Default` leaves it to Azure and ignores the value.
- `max_unavailable_value` (Number) Nodes Azure may take out of service at once during an upgrade — a node count, or a percentage of the pool between 0 and 100. Required when `max_unavailable_type` is not `Default`.
